Translational Gaps: No mammal has been engineered to secrete mussel foot protein 5 from its own epidermis, so the entire skin-as-glue framing rests on purified-protein biophysics rather than on any animal experiment. Recombinant production does not by itself give you an adhesive: the bacterium must also be given a tyrosinase, or the purified protein must be treated in vitro, because unmodified recombinant Mefp-5 lacking DOPA is markedly less adhesive than the native molecule. The headline -14 mJ/m(2) figure was measured between two identical mica surfaces in a surface forces apparatus, which means nobody has converted it into a lap-shear or peel strength on living tissue, and a card reader should not assume the two are interchangeable. The oxidation problem also remains unsolved in a body: any tissue-facing application has to hold the catechols reduced at physiological pH and oxygen tension long enough for them to bond.
Key References (DOIs): Danner Biochemistry 2012 https://doi.org/10.1021/bi3002538
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: A structural mislabelling is easy to make here and worth stating plainly. Protein Data Bank entry 7QAB is an NMR structure of Pvfp-5b, the homologous foot protein 5 of the green mussel Perna viridis, and it is not a structure of Mytilus edulis Mefp-5; it must not be presented as one. An AlphaFold model does exist for UniProt Q8WTE8 (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q8WTE8), but because the protein is intrinsically disordered by nature the model is low-confidence by construction rather than by accident, and computed disorder for this sequence runs to 75.5%. On availability: recombinant mussel adhesive protein is a purchasable reagent today rather than a therapeutic. Kollodis BioSciences (https://www.kollodis.com) produces it in a proprietary Escherichia coli system and sells it under the MAPTrix trademark as coating solutions, extracellular-matrix-mimetic reagents and 3D culture hydrogels, resold through Sigma-Aldrich and AMSBIO, with supplier datasheets listing a ~24,000 Da recombinant protein supplied at 0.2, 0.5 or 1.0 mg/mL (https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/product/sigma/161052k). It is a research-use reagent and not an approved drug or device, and no registered clinical trial administers mussel foot protein to humans. Note also that this route to adhesion is chemically opposite to the gecko route already in this library: setal beta-keratin sticks by dry van der Waals contact and fails underwater, whereas Mefp-5 forms actual chemical bonds to a wet surface.

Narrative: In the aftermath of Chernobyl, biologists found fungi growing directly on the ruined reactor walls. These black fungi, rich in melanin, seemed not just to tolerate gamma radiation but to thrive in it. Ekaterina Dadachova's 2007 paper proposed radiosynthesis — fungi literally eating radiation the way plants eat sunlight. A 2020 ISS experiment found Cladosporium grew 21% faster in orbit and blocked a small fraction of cosmic radiation. Tyrosinase-transfected hamster cells make their own melanin and resist gamma rays and UVA (though they become more sensitive to UVC). The radiotrophy claim, however, remains contested: critics argue that passive shielding plus oxidative-stress relief explains the observations without invoking a new form of metabolism. Melanin definitely absorbs radiation and scavenges free radicals — both well-established. Whether it does anything more exotic than that, decades later, still isn't settled. And melanized human melanomas are stubbornly radioresistant, which is an unhappy reminder of the double-edge.
Short Description: Cells engineered with tyrosinase make eumelanin, a dark pigment that absorbs radiation and mops up free radicals before they shred DNA. Chernobyl fungus with this pigment grew 1.21× faster on the ISS, and a 1.7mm layer blocked 2.17% of incoming radiation. Only tested in fungi and hamster cells — no mammal carries this pathway; mice only got injected nanoparticles. Those same pigmented cells turned more sensitive to UVC, and melanin is also what makes melanoma tumors radioresistant.
Mechanism: Melanin polymer; proposed "radiosynthesis" via IR-induced electronic-property changes (contested); well-established passive shielding + ROS scavenging.
Achievements (effect sizes): Dadachova 2007 PLoS ONE: melanized fungi at ~500× background IR grew faster than controls; ESR signal shifts; ~3× 14C-acetate incorporation; ~4× increase in NADH reduction capacity. Averesch/Shunk 2022 Front Microbiol: ISS experiment; Cladosporium fungal lawn ~1.7 mm thick attenuated ionizing radiation ~2.17% ± 0.25%; growth rate 1.21× ground; 21 cm extrapolated Mars shielding. Kaur/Hill 2001: tyrosinase pcTYR transfected CHOK1 cells produced eumelanin; resistant to 137Cs γ-ray + UVA killing; MORE SENSITIVE to UVC. Schweitzer 2010, Kunwar 2012, Rageh 2015: melanin nanoparticles (IP/IV) in BALB/c mice pre/post 7 Gy → reduced hematotoxicity, organ damage — EXOGENOUS delivery, not biosynthesis.
Highest Evidence Tier: T3 (heterologous tyrosinase in CHO) + T4/T5 for exogenous nanoparticles
Translational Gaps: Full DHN-melanin pathway in mammalian cells; transgenic animal; clinical trials.
Key References (DOIs): Dadachova PLoS ONE 2007 https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0000457 | Averesch Front Microbiol 2022 https://doi.org/10.3389/fmicb.2022.877625
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: RADIOTROPHY HYPOTHESIS CONTESTED: Walberg 2017 thesis and multiple reviews attribute observations to passive shielding + oxidative stress relief; Averesch 2022 softened to "radioadaptive." CONTRADICTION: Hopwood 1985 — exogenous melanin loaded endocytically into CHO gave NO radioprotection, contradicts Kaur 2001. Melanotic human melanomas are radioresistant (clinical double-edged sword). Kaur/Hill showed UVC INCREASED sensitivity (wavelength-specific). Not a single gene — requires copper/TRP1/TRP2/melanosome machinery.

Narrative: This is the only gene on this list that has actually saved human lives in a clinical trial. MGMT repairs a specific kind of chemotherapy-induced DNA damage, and a lab-engineered variant called P140K is resistant to a drug that shuts off the tumor's own MGMT. The strategy, pioneered by Jennifer Adair at Fred Hutch: take the patient's bone-marrow stem cells, install MGMT-P140K with a lentivirus, infuse them back, then give chemotherapy. The healthy stem cells now out-survive the tumor. In seven patients with an aggressive glioblastoma subtype (NCT00669669), median survival reached roughly 20 months versus the historical 12. Engraftment was durable. The caveats are serious: a pediatric version of the trial failed to produce lasting engraftment, and some integration clones raised concern about eventual leukemia. And endogenous MGMT in tumors is itself a villain — the gene cuts both ways depending on which cell it lives in.
Short Description: This gene repairs a chemo-induced DNA lesion, letting bone-marrow stem cells survive drugs that would wipe them out. In a 7-patient glioblastoma trial, median survival hit ~20 months versus a 12-month historical baseline. It's been tested in humans (NCT00669669) using the patient's own engineered stem cells infused back after treatment. Tradeoff: a pediatric version of the trial failed, with only transient engraftment in 4 of 7 children and no chemoprotection.
Mechanism: Suicide direct-reversal repair of O6-alkyl-guanine; P140K variant ~240× resistant to O6-benzylguanine inhibitor, enabling in vivo chemoselection of transduced HSCs.
Achievements (effect sizes): **THE ONLY GENE IN THIS LIBRARY WITH PEER-REVIEWED HUMAN CLINICAL EFFICACY DATA.** Adair 2012 Sci Transl Med: n=3 MGMT-unmethylated GBM; lentiviral P140K-transduced autologous CD34+; in-vivo selection during chemo; all 3 exceeded historical median OS (~12 mo); one >2-year PFS. Adair 2014 JCI (NCT00669669, n=7): median OS ~20 mo vs historical ~12 mo in MGMTu-GBM; polyclonal engraftment; PRDM16 and HMGA2 integration clones without adverse events. Dog/NHP long-term engraftment precedents.
Highest Evidence Tier: T7 (human clinical trial)
Translational Gaps: Phase III trial; CRISPR-HDR / prime-editing replacement for lentivirus to reduce integration clonality; broader indications beyond TMZ-treated MGMTu-GBM.
Key References (DOIs): Adair Sci Transl Med 2012 https://doi.org/10.1126/scitranslmed.3003541 | Adair JCI 2014 https://doi.org/10.1172/jci76739 | Kramer Hum Gene Ther 2018 https://doi.org/10.1089/hum.2017.235
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: FAILURE IN PEDIATRIC TRIAL: Kramer 2018 — only transient low-level engraftment in 4/7 pediatric patients; no chemoprotection. Integration clones (PRDM16, HMGA2) flagged but no leukemia to date. ALKYLATION-SPECIFIC — does NOT protect against ionizing radiation or oxidative damage. DOUBLE-EDGED: endogenous MGMT overexpression in tumors is a POOR-PROGNOSIS TMZ-resistance marker — gene is protective in HSCs but pathogenic in glioma; O6BG co-dosing required for chemoselection but causes its own toxicity.

Narrative: Belgian Blue cattle look like bodybuilders because they are — naturally. A deletion in their myostatin gene, discovered by McPherron and Lee at Johns Hopkins in 1997, removes the molecular brake on muscle growth. Without functional myostatin, skeletal muscle proliferates dramatically: Belgian Blues carry 20–25% more muscle fibers than normal cattle. The same biology works across species. In 2007, Mosher identified a myostatin mutation in racing Whippets — dogs heterozygous for the deletion were the fastest racers, while homozygotes were comically over-muscled 'bully Whippets'. In 2004, Schuelke reported the first known human myostatin mutation: a German boy born to a former professional sprinter carried a splice-site mutation in both MSTN alleles and showed visible muscle hypertrophy at birth, with quadriceps cross-section nearly twice normal at age four. He was otherwise healthy. The therapeutic angle is clear — blocking myostatin could treat muscular dystrophies, sarcopenia, and cachexia. Multiple antibody therapies have entered clinical trials, and CRISPR-mediated MSTN knockout has been demonstrated in pigs, dogs, and primates. The catch: myostatin also regulates tendons, cardiac muscle, and metabolism, and hyper-muscular animals often have calving difficulties and altered fat distribution.
Short Description: A secreted protein clamps down on muscle stem cells, blocking them from dividing and growing new fibers. Knock it out and mice gain 200–300% more muscle mass, with individual muscles 2–3 times heavier. No human gene therapy exists — the only case is a German boy with a natural mutation, quadriceps twice normal size at age 4.5. Antibody drugs for the same pathway failed in muscular dystrophy trials, and hyper-muscled Belgian Blue cattle need near-universal C-sections to give birth.
Mechanism: Myostatin (GDF-8): secreted TGF-beta family ligand; binds ActRIIB → SMAD2/3 phosphorylation → repression of MyoD/myogenin transcription and satellite cell proliferation. Loss-of-function → unrestricted myoblast proliferation and myofiber hypertrophy; fiber count increases (hyperplasia) and fiber size increases (hypertrophy).
Achievements (effect sizes): McPherron 1997 Nature: MSTN-null mice → muscle mass +200–300% vs wild-type (individual muscles 2–3× heavier). Belgian Blue cattle: +20–25% muscle fiber number (hyperplasia). Schuelke 2004 NEJM: human MSTN-null boy — quadriceps CSA ~2× normal at age 4.5; grossly muscular at birth. Mosher 2007: heterozygous Whippets were fastest racers; homozygous 'bully' phenotype. Lee 2012: MSTN-null mice had reduced body fat (~50% less adipose tissue).
Highest Evidence Tier: T6
Translational Gaps: No human gene-therapy trial for MSTN-KO; antibody therapies (domagrozumab, stamulumab) had disappointing phase II results in DMD; CRISPR-KO in primates showed mosaicism; tendon/ligament adaptation to hyper-muscular loads; cardiac effects of systemic MSTN loss; long-term metabolic consequences.
Key References (DOIs): McPherron Nature 1997 https://doi.org/10.1038/387083a0 | Schuelke NEJM 2004 https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa040933 | Mosher PLoS Genet 2007 https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pgen.0030079
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: Myostatin antibodies (stamulumab, domagrozumab) FAILED to show clinical benefit in DMD phase II trials — systemic myostatin inhibition may not be enough when muscle is already dystrophic. Hyper-muscular cattle have dystocia (difficult births) and Belgian Blues require near-universal C-sections. MSTN-null mice have altered glucose metabolism and reduced adipose, which could be benefit or risk depending on context. The one known human case is a single individual — long-term health outcomes unknown. CRISPR-edited MSTN-KO pigs and dogs show variable mosaicism.

Manipulation: overexpression (feather-epithelium-restricted; the loss-of-function allele is the single substitution R644W)
Narrative:
Almost every bright yellow or red vertebrate is wearing borrowed colour. Flamingos, goldfinches, salmon flesh, the red of a house finch's breast: all of it is dietary carotenoid, absorbed from food and deposited, which is why a captive flamingo fades without supplemented feed. Parrots are the exception, and they had been the exception for a long time before anyone knew why. Parrot feathers are coloured by psittacofulvins, pigments found in no other bird lineage, and parrots make them themselves.

The gene was found through pet birds. Budgerigar breeders have maintained a recessive 'blue' line for a century, in which the yellow pigment is simply absent and the bird's structural blue shows through unmodified. Treating that as a Mendelian genetics problem, a genome-wide scan across wild-type and blue budgerigars put the locus in a single region of chromosome 1, and the causal change turned out to be one amino acid substitution in an enzyme nobody expected to find in a bird: a type I polyketide synthase, a class of enzyme normally associated with bacterial and fungal natural-product chemistry (Cooke 2017, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.08.016). Expressing the budgerigar enzyme in yeast produced the pigments, and mass spectrometry matched them to the compounds in real feathers.

For an enhancement library, the appeal is autonomy: colour that does not depend on what you ate. The catch is that the coding sequence is the cheap part. Chicken and crow both carry functional homologues of the same enzyme, and both are unpigmented by it, because what distinguishes the budgerigar is a colossal transcriptional upregulation in feather epithelium rather than a better enzyme. There is a further biological constraint that no amount of promoter engineering removes. The pigment is made in axial-plate keratinocytes that then die by programmed cell death as the feather barb splits open, so in the bird the pigment factory is a cell lineage that is built to terminate. Where the pigment would end up in a hairless, non-feathered animal is not something anyone has tested.
Short Description: Your skin builds its own yellow pigment from scratch instead of extracting it from food, so hair and skin turn vivid yellow on any diet, including one with no carotenoids in it at all. The enzyme is a polyketide synthase that chains malonyl-CoA units into linear conjugated polyenes, and in a regenerating budgerigar feather it runs in the top 2.7% of all genes by expression, against 1.1% for the structural feather keratin KRT75. Across 280 genotyped birds a single arginine-to-tryptophan change at residue 644 segregated perfectly with colour: every blue budgerigar was homozygous for it. This has only ever been done in a parrot and reconstituted in yeast, with no mammalian attempt on record. The hard limit is regulatory rather than genetic, since chicken and crow carry working copies of the gene and stay unpigmented for want of the hundreds-to-thousands-fold feather upregulation.
Mechanism: MuPKS is a metazoan type I polyketide synthase, a multidomain enzyme of the class better known from bacterial and fungal secondary metabolism. Instead of modifying a carotenoid taken from the diet, it condenses malonyl-coenzyme A (malonyl-CoA) units into linear conjugated polyene chains, the psittacofulvin pigments, synthesised de novo in feather epithelium. This is the reason parrots are the vertebrate exception: nearly all other bright yellow and red vertebrates require dietary carotenoid precursors, whereas a parrot manufactures its own chromophore. The loss-of-function allele behind the blue morph substitutes tryptophan for arginine at residue 644, inside the malonyl-CoA:acyl-carrier-protein transacylase (MAT) domain that loads the malonyl extender unit; the equivalent conserved arginine forms a salt bridge with the C-3 carboxylate of malonyl-CoA, and mutating that arginine to alanine caused a 100-fold decrease in MAT domain activity in recombinant human fatty-acid synthase. Colour output, however, depends on regulatory upregulation of the gene in feather epithelium and not on the coding sequence alone.
Achievements (effect sizes): The genetic evidence is unusually clean for a pigmentation trait. Sanger sequencing of the R644W site across the full budgerigar sample set showed that all 162 WT birds had genotype R/R or R/W, whereas all 118 blue birds had genotype W/W, which is complete segregation of a coding variant with the phenotype under a recessive model in 280 genotyped animals (Cooke 2017, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.08.016). That variant was reached by mapping rather than by candidate guessing: reduced-representation genome sequencing of wild-type against blue birds localised the Mendelian blue locus to a single region of chromosome 1 with a highly significant association signal (p = 10 -72 , Fisher's exact test) (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.08.016). Messenger RNA sequencing of regenerating contour feathers then showed how hard the gene is being driven: expression of MuPKS is in the top 2.7% of genes genome wide, which the authors compare directly against KRT75, a structural feather keratin, at the top 1.1% (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.08.016). The cross-species comparison supplies the decisive control, because budgerigar MuPKS was expressed hundreds to thousands of times higher than its homologs in chicken and crow, neither of which shows psittacofulvin pigmentation despite carrying the gene (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.08.016). Finally, heterologous expression in yeast reconstituted pigment synthesis outright, with the products matched to feather pigments by mass spectrometry.
Highest Evidence Tier: T5 (Mendelian mapping in 280 genotyped birds, complete allele segregation, plus heterologous reconstitution of pigment synthesis in yeast confirmed by mass spectrometry)
Translational Gaps: No mammalian expression of this enzyme has been attempted, so there is no evidence at all about whether a mouse or a human keratinocyte can carry the pathway. The yeast reconstitution establishes that the enzyme alone is sufficient to make the pigment in a eukaryotic cell, but the study reports no titre in milligrams per litre, so nobody knows how much pigment a heterologous host can actually accumulate. Deposition is the deeper unknown: in the bird the pigment may be transferred onto the growing feather from the axial plate rather than synthesised in place within the pigmented structure, which means an animal without feathers has no obvious equivalent route for getting the pigment where it would be visible. Because the phenotype is driven by transcript level rather than by protein sequence, recreating it requires a promoter and enhancer context that delivers hundreds-to-thousands-fold upregulation in the right cell layer, and no such regulatory cassette has been built.
Key References (DOIs): Cooke Cell 2017 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.08.016
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: There is no UniProt entry for MuPKS. Searching the NCBI protein records for Melopsittacus undulatus returns fatty-acid synthase and other unrelated entries rather than this enzyme, and there is no Protein Data Bank structure, so every structural claim about the malonyl-CoA:acyl-carrier-protein transacylase active site is an inference from homologous fatty-acid synthase rather than a solved parrot structure (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.08.016). The underlying sequencing data are public: reduced-representation and messenger RNA sequencing are deposited at the Sequence Read Archive under PRJNA378643 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJNA378643) and the chromatin-conformation data under PRJNA378785 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJNA378785). Melopsittacus undulatus is already represented in this database through the short-wavelength opsin card, but no pigment-synthesis gene from it was present before this entry. There is no commercial or clinical activity of any kind: a registry search for psittacofulvin returns no trials, and no supplier sells the enzyme or the pigment. It is worth separating this card from the melanin entry in the same library, which is a passive reactive-oxygen-scavenging polymer framed for radiation shielding; MuPKS is a biosynthetic route to a different polymer class, and it is chemical absorbance rather than the thin-film interference used by reflectin and tapetum cards.

Narrative: The Japanese fire-belly newt (Cynops pyrrhogaster) can regenerate entire limbs, lenses, retina, and heart tissue throughout its life — a superpower lost in most vertebrates. Newtic1 is a newt-specific gene encoding a protein that triggers dedifferentiation of mature cells back into progenitor states, specifically through erythrocyte clumping at wound sites. It represents a molecular switch for regeneration that evolution has kept locked in mammals.
Short Description: Blood cells clump at the wound, forming a scaffold that coaxes nearby mature cells to forget their identity and rebuild a lens from scratch. This gene has zero orthologs outside urodele amphibians — humans carry no equivalent copy. It's only ever worked in the Japanese fire-belly newt, nowhere near a human trial. The tradeoff: with no mammalian version to borrow safety limits from, the therapy risks uncontrolled cell proliferation at the injury site.
Mechanism: Newtic1 protein promotes clumping of erythrocytes at wound sites in the lens regeneration zone, creating a cellular scaffold. It triggers dedifferentiation of terminally differentiated cells by activating stemness transcription factors, enabling re-entry into the cell cycle and subsequent transdifferentiation into the required tissue type.
Achievements (effect sizes): Newtic1 expression is essential for lens regeneration in adult newts. Clumped erythrocytes expressing Newtic1 contribute to regenerating tissue. The gene has no orthologs outside urodele amphibians.
Highest Evidence Tier: T3
Translational Gaps: No mammalian ortholog exists; full pathway may require multiple newt-specific factors. Risk of uncontrolled proliferation. Delivery to injury sites in a controlled, transient manner is critical.
Key References (DOIs): https://doi.org/10.1038/srep36380
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: Newtic1 is specific to urodele amphibians and involves erythrocyte clumping at wound sites, not lens regeneration directly.

Manipulation: Recombinant protein administration (cenegermin, rhNGF 20 µg/mL) — topical
Narrative:
The cornea is the most densely innervated surface on the human body, and those nerves are not only there to hurt. Trigeminal sensory axons and the corneal epithelium keep each other alive: the epithelium releases nerve growth factor for the nerves, and the nerves release substance P and insulin-like growth factor 1 back for the epithelium. Cut that loop — by herpes simplex or zoster keratitis, by diabetes, by neurosurgery near the trigeminal ganglion — and you get neurotrophic keratitis: a cornea that cannot feel, will not re-epithelialise, and progresses through persistent defect to ulcer, corneal melt and perforation. Because the eye is numb, patients do not complain until the damage is advanced.

Cenegermin is recombinant human nerve growth factor put straight onto the ocular surface, six drops a day for eight weeks, replacing the missing ligand at the site where it is needed. Two double-masked vehicle-controlled trials — REPARO in Europe with 156 patients and NGF0214 in the United States with 48 — both hit their healing endpoints with masked central readers grading lesion closure (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ophtha.2018.02.022, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ophtha.2019.08.020). A 2026 meta-analysis of the pair reports a pooled relative risk of 1.84 for complete healing and rates the certainty of the evidence moderate under GRADE (https://doi.org/10.1177/25158414261460347). It reached market as OXERVATE, the first topical biologic for the condition.

The pharmacological irony is worth sitting with. Nerve growth factor is the canonical pain neurotrophin, and one of the larger analgesia programmes of the last two decades — tanezumab and its relatives — consisted of antibodies designed to neutralise exactly this protein in osteoarthritic joints. Here the same molecule is deliberately supplied, and the desired effect and the side effect are the same biology: an eye that can feel again is an eye that can hurt again. A cenegermin trial in neuropathic corneal pain at Tufts was withdrawn (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05700864). Phase 3 work continues in persistent corneal epithelial defects of other causes and, delivered intranasally, in ischaemic optic neuropathy.
Short Description: Eye drops that regrow the sensory nerves of a numb, ulcerating cornea, so a hole in the front of the eye closes and the eye can feel again. In the pivotal US trial 16 of 23 treated patients (69.6%) healed their corneal lesion against 7 of 24 on vehicle (29.2%), a difference of 40.4% (95% CI, 14.2%-66.6%; P = 0.006), and a meta-analysis of the two masked trials puts the number needed to treat at 3 (95% CI 2-5). This is the only gene in the Regeneration set you can actually buy: it is sold today as OXERVATE, approved by the European Medicines Agency in 2017 and the US Food and Drug Administration in 2018 for moderate-to-severe neurotrophic keratitis. The catch is that nerve growth factor is the same molecule that anti-NGF drugs were built to block for arthritis pain, so restoring sensation restores pain — eye pain was the most common drug-related adverse event in a Chinese phase IV cohort, in 5 of 28 patients (17.9%).
Mechanism: Beta nerve growth factor (β-NGF) is a neurotrophin translated as a 241-amino-acid pro-form and secreted as a homodimer, signalling through the high-affinity receptor tropomyosin receptor kinase A (TrkA, encoded by NTRK1) and the low-affinity receptor p75NTR. On the ocular surface the trigeminal sensory axons and the corneal epithelium run a reciprocal trophic loop: epithelium-derived NGF sustains the nerves, while nerve-derived substance P and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) sustain the epithelium. Damage to the trigeminal pathway from herpes simplex or zoster keratitis, diabetes or neurosurgery breaks that loop and produces neurotrophic keratitis, an anaesthetic cornea that fails to re-epithelialise and progresses to ulceration, melt and perforation. Topical recombinant human NGF (cenegermin) supplies the missing ligand directly, driving TrkA-dependent axonal regrowth from the surviving subbasal nerve plexus together with epithelial proliferation and wound closure. This is regeneration rather than lubrication, and the endpoints reflect that: the trials measured lesion closure and recovery of corneal sensitivity (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ophtha.2018.02.022).
Achievements (effect sizes): In REPARO, a multicentre randomised double-masked vehicle-controlled trial of 156 patients with stage 2 or stage 3 neurotrophic keratitis in one eye treated with six drops a day for eight weeks, at week 4 (primary end point), 19.6% of vehicle-treated patients achieved corneal healing (<0.5-mm lesion staining) versus 54.9% receiving rhNGF 10 μg/ml (+35.3%; 97.06% CI, 15.88-54.71; P < 0.001) and 58.0% receiving rhNGF 20 μg/ml (+38.4%; 97.06% CI, 18.96-57.83; P < 0.001), and at week 8, 43.1% of vehicle vs 74.5% receiving 10 μg/ml (+31.4%; 97.06% CI, 11.25-51.49; P = 0.001) and 74.0% receiving 20 μg/ml (+30.9%; 97.06% CI, 10.60-51.13; P = 0.002); more than 96% of patients who healed remained recurrence free during follow-up (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ophtha.2018.02.022). The pivotal US trial NGF0214 replicated this across 11 sites in 48 patients: compared to 7 of 24 vehicle-treated patients (29.2%), 16 of 23 cenegermin-treated patients (69.6%) achieved less than 0.5 mm of lesion staining (+40.4%; 95% CI, 14.2%-66.6%; P = 0.006), and by the conservative measure, compared to 4 of 24 vehicle-treated patients (16.7%), 15 of 23 cenegermin-treated patients (65.2%) achieved 0 mm of lesion staining and no other residual staining (+48.6%; 95% CI, 24.0%-73.1%; P < 0.001) (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ophtha.2019.08.020). Pooling both trials across 148 adults gave a pooled RR of 1.84 (95% CI 1.34-2.52; z = 3.8; p = 0.0001) for complete corneal healing at 8 weeks, a model-based pooled risk difference of 0.42 (95% CI 0.24-0.60), an NNT of 3 (95% CI 2-5), crude pooled event rates of 72.6% cenegermin versus 38.7% vehicle, and a pooled RR for any adverse event of 1.07 (95% CI 0.64-1.78; p = 0.80), with zero heterogeneity and moderate GRADE certainty (https://doi.org/10.1177/25158414261460347). Post-approval use held up in a prospective Chinese phase IV cohort of 28 patients, where 22/26 (84.6%, 95% confidence interval 65.1-95.6%; 2 missing) achieved corneal healing at week 8, 3/22 (13.6%) reported recurrence during 48-week follow-up but 20/22 (90.9%) were healed at week 56, while 2/28 (7.1%) experienced lesion worsening during 8-week treatment (https://doi.org/10.1007/s40123-025-01253-5).
Highest Evidence Tier: T10 (two positive double-masked RCTs, moderate-GRADE meta-analysis, EMA and FDA approved and sold today)
Translational Gaps: The biology is settled for this indication, so what is missing is mostly access and scope. Cenegermin is among the most expensive topical drugs per course of treatment, and a 2025 review of NGF therapeutics lists high treatment cost, limited long-term data and potential proangiogenic effects on the ocular surface as the unresolved issues. Healing is not permanent in everyone: 3 of 22 healed patients (13.6%) relapsed during 48-week follow-up in the phase IV cohort (https://doi.org/10.1007/s40123-025-01253-5). The regenerative claim is currently proven only where trigeminal denervation is the cause, because the trials that would extend it to persistent corneal epithelial defects of other aetiology (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07519902) and to optic-nerve disease by the intranasal route (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07453888) are both still recruiting. And because the drug is deliberately topical, nothing here tells us what supplying NGF would do to the TrkA-bearing sensory and sympathetic neurons of the rest of the body.
Key References (DOIs): Bonini Ophthalmology 2018 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ophtha.2018.02.022 | Pflugfelder Ophthalmology 2020 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ophtha.2019.08.020 | Faroog Therapeutic Advances in Ophthalmology 2026 https://doi.org/10.1177/25158414261460347 | Li Ophthalmology and Therapy 2025 https://doi.org/10.1007/s40123-025-01253-5
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: The direction of every listed trial was checked: all of them administer NGF as the therapeutic agent, which is the opposite of the large anti-NGF analgesia programmes such as tanezumab and fasinumab that were built to block the same protein in osteoarthritic joints. That opposition is the tradeoff rather than a contradiction in the data, and it is worth surfacing on the card. Two registered studies must not be read as evidence of benefit because neither ever ran: the neuropathic corneal pain trial at Tufts Medical Center was withdrawn (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05700864), as was a study of corneal thickness by anterior-segment optical coherence tomography (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06411145). The safety profile in real-world use is heavier than the pooled adverse-event risk ratio suggests: in the Chinese phase IV cohort 25 of 28 patients (89.3%) had at least one treatment-emergent adverse event and 10 (35.7%) had serious ones, though none were assessed as related to cenegermin, and eye pain was the most common drug-related event at 5 of 28 (17.9%) (https://doi.org/10.1007/s40123-025-01253-5). Commercially this is the one entry in the Regeneration set that a person can be prescribed today: Dompé Farmaceutici markets it as OXERVATE (cenegermin-bkbj) 0.002% ophthalmic solution, approved by the European Medicines Agency in 2017 and the US Food and Drug Administration in 2018 with orphan designation, dosed at 20 µg/mL six times daily for eight weeks (https://www.dompe.com).

Narrative: Bird cones each carry a droplet of oil at their tip, coloured red, yellow or clear, sitting exactly where light must pass on its way to the visual pigment. For decades these were understood as filters that sharpen the boundaries between cone classes, but nobody knew what the pale ones were made of or how a retina built them. Toomey and colleagues worked out both. The relevant pigments are apocarotenoids, cleavage products of the dietary carotenoid zeaxanthin, and the retina makes them with three enzymes acting in sequence: beta-carotene oxygenase 2 cuts zeaxanthin, a retinol dehydrogenase reduces the fragment to galloxanthin, and retinol saturase saturates one bond to give dihydrogalloxanthin (https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.15675). They proved the route by assembling it in cultured human kidney cells: the first enzyme alone gave a product absorbing at 449 nm, adding the second gave galloxanthin, and adding the third, cloned from zebra finch, gave the finished dihydrogalloxanthin. Then they asked what the filter is for, by modelling colour discrimination across 18 bird species and letting the droplet's cutoff wavelength vary freely. The model settled on 425.1 +/- 6.5 nm for ultraviolet-sensitive birds and 457.4 +/- 9.7 nm for violet-sensitive ones, and those optima landed within 2 per cent of the number of discriminable colours the real birds achieve. In other words the retina has tuned its internal filters to match its own opsins almost exactly, and shifting the ratio of the two apocarotenoids is how it does the tuning. This is a striking thing to consider installing in a human eye, because it is not a new photopigment but a new piece of optics grown inside a cell, and it only pays off if the pigment behind it has been moved to match. It is also the one candidate here whose failure mode is chemical: the first enzyme normally exists to destroy carotenoids, and blocking that job elsewhere in the body has consequences of its own.
Short Description: A coloured oil bead grows inside each cone cell and sits directly in that cone's light path, acting as a private lens-filter that strips short wavelengths before they reach the pigment behind it. Sharpening colour boundaries this way is what separates the two grades of bird vision: ultraviolet-sensitive birds are modelled to discriminate 8.24 +/- 1.77 million colours against 5.18 +/- 1.03 million for violet-sensitive ones. The whole three-enzyme pathway has been rebuilt from scratch in cultured human kidney cells, which turned dietary zeaxanthin into the finished filter pigment, but no animal has ever been engineered to grow an oil droplet. A filter throws photons away, so the discrimination gain holds only in bright light and collapses as luminance falls toward the 0.025 to 0.1 candela per square metre dark-noise limit. Install the filter without also shifting the matching cone opsin and you open a blind spot between 400 and 450 nm where discrimination gets substantially worse.
Mechanism: This is a defined three-enzyme program acting on dietary zeaxanthin. Beta-carotene oxygenase 2 (BCO2) cleaves zeaxanthin to 3-hydroxy-10'-apo-beta-caroten-10'-al; retinol dehydrogenase 12 (RDH12) reduces that aldehyde to the alcohol galloxanthin; and retinol saturase (RETSAT) saturates the 11',12' bond to yield 11',12'-dihydrogalloxanthin. Both apocarotenoids accumulate inside the C-type oil droplet of the short-wavelength-sensitive 2 (SWS2) cone and of the double cone, where they function as intracellular short-pass spectral filters positioned upstream of the visual pigment. Changing the ratio of galloxanthin to dihydrogalloxanthin moves the droplet's spectral cutoff wavelength, and that mobile cutoff is what keeps the SWS2 cone spectrally adjacent to an SWS1 cone whose own peak has been shifted into either the ultraviolet or the violet. Transcript levels of all three enzymes rise significantly across retinal development, tracking the accumulation of the apocarotenoids themselves.
Achievements (effect sizes): The pathway was rebuilt from its parts in cultured human kidney cells. Cells expressing beta-carotene oxygenase 2 alone yielded a product with a characteristic single absorbance peak at 449 nm; adding retinol dehydrogenase 12 yielded galloxanthin; and adding zebra finch retinol saturase, with zeaxanthin supplied in the medium, yielded dihydrogalloxanthin, establishing that these three enzymes are sufficient to produce dihydrogalloxanthin from zeaxanthin (Toomey 2016, https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.15675). Measurement of the natural droplet backed this up: the C-type oil droplet of the violet-sensitive chicken contained galloxanthin with a peak absorbance at 402 nm plus an apocarotenoid of undetermined structure peaking at 380 nm, with the fitted spectra consisting primarily of galloxanthin and dihydrogalloxanthin and every other carotenoid contributing 9 per cent or less to the best fit. Receptor-noise-limited discrimination modelling in bright light, sweeping the droplet cutoff from 370 to 500 nm in 6 nm steps, found an optimal cutoff of 425.1 +/- 6.5 nm for the 11 ultraviolet-sensitive species against 457.4 +/- 9.7 nm for the 7 violet-sensitive ones, a significant difference (t = -7.78, p = 2.13 x 10^-5), and the modelled optima differed from the birds' actual parameters by only 2 per cent in the number of discriminable colours. Using each species' real measured parameters, ultraviolet-sensitive birds came out at 8.24 +/- 1.77 x 10^6 discriminable colours against 5.18 +/- 1.03 x 10^6 for violet-sensitive birds (t = 4.74, p = 0.00021, https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.15675).
Highest Evidence Tier: T4 (biochemical reconstitution of the full pathway in HEK293 cells, chemical identification of the apocarotenoids by HPLC and derivatization, a developmental expression time course, and colour-vision modelling across 18 species)
Translational Gaps: Mammalian retinas contain no oil droplets and offer no organelle that could hold apocarotenoids in the light path of a single cone, so the filter has nowhere to sit even if the enzymes worked. Making galloxanthin without a droplet to sequester it invites the opposite problem, because beta-carotene oxygenase 2 normally degrades carotenoids and losing that function lets them build up. Human vision is trichromatic, which means there is no fourth cone class for a matched filter to serve, while the modelled discrimination gain assumes a tetrachromatic cone mosaic throughout. No animal of any kind has been engineered to gain an oil droplet, so the entire phenotype rests on biochemistry in a dish plus modelling of wild birds.
Key References (DOIs): Toomey eLife 2016 https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.15675 | Twyman BMC Evolutionary Biology 2018 https://doi.org/10.1186/s12862-018-1136-y
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: The reconstitution was assembled across species and the record should say so plainly: beta-carotene oxygenase 2 and retinol dehydrogenase 12 were cloned from 21-day-old chicken retina, and only retinol saturase came from adult zebra finch retina, which is why the zebra finch is listed here as the ultraviolet-sensitive source species (Toomey 2016, https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.15675). The 402 nm galloxanthin peak was likewise measured in the violet-sensitive chicken rather than in a UV-sensitive bird. Two facts should temper any enthusiasm for installing this. First, deficiency of beta-carotene oxygenase 2 in mouse or zebrafish produces over-accumulation of carotenoids that induces oxidative stress and cell death, so the pathway is only benign where its products are captured and sequestered in a droplet as they are in the avian retina. Second, the filter has to match its opsin: giving an ultraviolet-sensitive visual system a violet-type C-type droplet produces a spectral blind spot between 400 and 450 nm where discrimination is substantially reduced, so a mismatched installation makes vision worse. Structural and sequence resources are thin. There is no experimental structure for any of the three enzymes; UniProt carries zebra finch BCO2 as H0YPV0 (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/H0YPV0) and zebra finch RETSAT as H0YZL4 (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/H0YZL4), both with AlphaFold models, while a gene-name search returned no chicken RDH12 entry. No trial exists. Registry searches on astaxanthin and retina return only oral antioxidant supplement studies in diabetic retinopathy and age-related macular degeneration, for instance NCT02062034 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02062034) and NCT03702374 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03702374) from the University of Guadalajara; those are carotenoid supplementation trials with no relationship to expressing this pathway, and they are recorded only to document the direction check. The 2018 comparative study extends the developmental and evolutionary picture (Twyman 2018, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12862-018-1136-y).

Narrative: Birds do not need their eyes to know what season it is. Blinded ducks and pinealectomised quail still answer lengthening days by growing their gonads, an observation that left a century-old question open: what inside the brain is catching the light? Nakane and colleagues at Nagoya (https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1006393107) answered it in 2010 by finding Opsin 5, also called neuropsin, in neurons of the paraventricular organ, cells that push a process into the third ventricle and sit directly in the cerebrospinal fluid, with fibres running to the median eminence beside the pars tuberalis. Expressed on its own in frog oocytes, the quail protein turned light into membrane current with a peak sensitivity near 420 nm, in the violet and near-ultraviolet. Then came the experiment that makes the trait real rather than suggestive. Quail had both eyes patched and the pineal gland removed, and were given two weeks of long days under ultraviolet-B, ultraviolet-A or blue light; their testes grew about as much as under ordinary white light. With every classical photoreceptive organ taken out of the loop, light was still arriving at the hypothalamus and being read there. The pathway it feeds is neuroendocrine rather than visual. Light-activated paraventricular neurons signal to the pars tuberalis, which switches on thyroid-stimulating hormone; that hormone induces type 2 deiodinase in the tanycytes lining the third ventricle, which converts thyroxine into the active thyroid hormone locally and opens the seasonal cascade that ends in gonadal growth. Installed in a human, this would be a photometer wired straight to the reproductive axis and buried under bone and hair, a sense whose sensitivity depends far less on the molecule than on how much violet light a skull lets through.
Short Description: Light detectors go onto neurons deep inside the brain, on the cells that bathe in cerebrospinal fluid at the floor of the hypothalamus, so violet and ultraviolet photons that make it through the skull are read by the brain itself rather than by the eyes. In quail with both eyes patched shut and the pineal gland surgically removed, two weeks of ultraviolet or blue long days still grew the testes by about as much as white light at 600 lux. The pigment peaks near 420 nm, in the violet band that scalp and skull attenuate most strongly, so a large-headed mammal would deliver far fewer usable photons to the same molecule than a quail does. This has only ever been shown in birds: no mammal has been given deep-brain light sensing, and no trial administers this receptor. Its output is not a percept but the reproductive axis, so the enhancement hands gonad size and seasonal hormone state to whatever light leaks through your skull.
Mechanism: Opsin 5 (OPN5), also called neuropsin, is an opsin-family G-protein-coupled receptor. In quail it is expressed in neurons of the paraventricular organ (PVO), a cluster whose cells contact the cerebrospinal fluid of the third ventricle and send fibres to the external zone of the median eminence next to the pars tuberalis (PT). Light absorbed by these PVO neurons is relayed to the pars tuberalis, which induces thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH); PT-derived TSH in turn induces type 2 deiodinase (DIO2) in the tanycytes lining the third ventricle, and DIO2 converts the prohormone thyroxine (T4) into the active hormone triiodothyronine (T3) locally inside the hypothalamus, triggering the photoperiodic neuroendocrine cascade that ends in gonadal growth. Heterologous expression establishes that the molecule itself is the sensor rather than a downstream relay: quail OPN5 in Xenopus oocytes produces light-dependent membrane currents whose action spectrum matches a retinal-based pigment.
Achievements (effect sizes): Quail Opsin 5 expressed in frog oocytes and recorded under two-electrode voltage clamp produced light-dependent membrane currents whose action spectrum closely matched that predicted for a retinal1-based pigment with a peak sensitivity at about 420 nm, measured as 419 nm and 418 nm in two independent experiments (Nakane 2010, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1006393107). The same recordings put a size on the response: the saturated current evoked by full-strength white light had a mean amplitude of 22 microamps, which the authors used as the ceiling when fitting the dose-response measured at 375 nm to a Hill function. The whole-animal test was the decisive one. Quail were eye-patched and pinealectomized, removing both retina and pineal organ from the light path, then held on a long-day schedule of 20 hours light and 4 hours dark for two weeks under ultraviolet-B, ultraviolet-A or blue light. Long-day stimulation with each of these short wavelengths induced testicular growth of a magnitude the authors describe as similar to that observed in birds exposed to white light at 600 lux (https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1006393107). Because the classical photoreceptive organs had been surgically excluded, the result places a functioning photoreceptor inside the brain itself rather than in any eye.
Highest Evidence Tier: T4 (in vivo avian physiology with surgical controls, eye-patched and pinealectomized, plus a heterologous action spectrum; no mammalian gain-of-function transfer)
Translational Gaps: Mammals do carry OPN5, with human accession Q6U736 and mouse Q6VZZ7, and they express it in the retina, the skin and the preoptic area, but no mammal has been shown to run seasonal reproduction off a deep-brain photoreceptor, so the circuit the quail data describe has no established mammalian counterpart. The limiting step in a human is optical rather than molecular: a thick skull, a large brain and hair attenuate violet and near-ultraviolet light heavily, and this receptor peaks near 420 nm, precisely where that attenuation bites hardest. Nobody has overexpressed OPN5 in a mammalian hypothalamus and demonstrated that the resulting neurons detect light, and nobody has shown what a mammalian brain would do with such a signal if it did arrive.
Key References (DOIs): Nakane Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 2010 https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1006393107
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: The action spectrum rests on two independent measurements that returned 419 nm and 418 nm, which the authors summarise as approximately 420 nm (Nakane 2010, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1006393107). That figure sits awkwardly beside the older literature the same authors cite: earlier action spectra for the quail photoperiodic response reported a peak around 483 to 492 nm, and Oishi had shown that 350 nm light also induced testicular growth. The authors accordingly describe Opsin 5 as one of the deep-brain photoreceptive molecules rather than the only one, and note that the spectral sensitivities of avian melanopsin and vertebrate-ancient (VA) opsin were still undetermined when they published. No human trial administers or targets OPN5. A registry keyword search returned only NCT06094504, 'Spectral Lighting and Intestinal Failure' at Cincinnati Children's, enrolling by invitation (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06094504); it is a spectral-lighting intervention that neither administers nor measures OPN5, and it is recorded here purely to document that the registry holds no genuine OPN5 trial, not as supporting evidence. No experimental structure of OPN5 exists; the quail sequence used here is UniProt D9N3D0 (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/D9N3D0).

Manipulation: Doxycycline-gated polycistronic transgene program (partial reprogramming; c-Myc deliberately omitted)
Narrative:
In 2006 Takahashi and Yamanaka showed that four transcription factors can walk an adult cell all the way back to an embryonic state (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2006.07.024). That is too far. A liver cell that forgets it is a liver cell is not rejuvenated, it is a tumour risk. The idea behind partial reprogramming is to start the journey and stop early — to erase the epigenetic marks a cell has accumulated over a lifetime while leaving its identity intact.

Yuancheng Lu and David Sinclair's group at Harvard Medical School built the minimum viable version: three of the four factors, with c-Myc deliberately omitted, packed as a single polycistron into one viral particle and placed behind a switch that only opens while the animal is receiving doxycycline. They injected it into the eye, because the retina lets you measure whether something worked by asking the animal what it can see.

It worked in three separate ways. After the optic nerve was crushed, twice as many retinal ganglion cells survived in 12-month-old mice — as many as in young ones. In middle-aged retinas, around 90% of the 464 genes that had drifted with age snapped back to their five-month-old levels. And most striking, in a glaucoma model where treatment was deliberately withheld until axons and cells had already been lost, the treated eye rebuilt its axon density to match the healthy eye and the animal recovered about half of its lost visual acuity. Read that number carefully: it is a return toward the pre-treatment baseline, not a doubling of normal vision.

The mechanism is not cell replacement — no new retinal ganglion cells appeared. It is demethylation, and it depends on the enzymes that do the erasing: knocking down either TET1 or TET2 abolishes the effect. Stoichiometry mattered too, in a way that reads like a warning to anyone reproducing it: delivering the three factors in three separate viruses did nothing at all for axon regeneration. Life Biosciences has taken this construct into a first-in-human Phase 1 for glaucoma and ischemic optic neuropathy, which makes this the library's only card with a recruiting anti-ageing trial — and the reason the 18-month-old mouse failure matters, because the human patients are old.
Short Description: Switches three embryonic transcription factors back on for a few weeks inside the surviving nerve cells of the eye, and they rewind their DNA methylation toward a younger pattern, regrow cut optic nerve fibres and recover sight that glaucoma had already destroyed. In 12-month-old mice, roughly 90% of the 464 genes whose expression had shifted with age were restored to youthful levels, and treatment begun after axons were already lost rebuilt axon density to that of the healthy eye. The three-factor construct is in people now: Life Biosciences' ER-100 is a recruiting Phase 1 in open-angle glaucoma and non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy with 5-year follow-up, 18 participants, safety as the primary endpoint. c-Myc is deliberately left out because continuous expression of all four factors in normal mice often induces teratomas or kills within days. The benefit is also age-capped: restoration of visual acuity was not seen in 18-month-old mice.
Mechanism: Three of the four Yamanaka factors — Oct4 (Pou5f1), Sox2 and Klf4, collectively OSK — are delivered as a single polycistron inside one adeno-associated virus (AAV) particle, under a tetracycline-response-element promoter, so expression switches on when the animal receives doxycycline and switches off when it does not. Omitting c-Myc and keeping induction partial is what prevents full dedifferentiation. OSK then drives active DNA demethylation through the ten-eleven translocation dioxygenases TET1 and TET2 — knockdown of either abolishes the effect — and through thymine DNA glycosylase (TDG)-dependent base excision, restoring youthful methylation across an ageing signature of 1,226 CpG sites and re-inducing Stat3. The mechanism is erasure of accumulated epigenetic noise rather than replacement of cells: treated 12-month-old mice showed no increase in retinal ganglion cell number and no increase in axon density beyond restoration, and no evidence of retinal ganglion cell proliferation was found.
Achievements (effect sizes): Retinal ganglion cells were purified by fluorescence-activated cell sorting from 12-month-old mice, treated or untreated with four weeks of doxycycline-induced OSK, and compared by RNA sequencing against cells from 5-month-old young mice: 464 genes had been altered during ageing (268 downregulated, 196 upregulated), and remarkably, around 90% of them were restored to youthful levels by OSK treatment (Lu 2020, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2975-4). In the optic-nerve-crush injury model, OSK treatment doubled retinal ganglion cell survival in 12-month-old mice, similar to what was observed in 1- and 3-month-old mice, and the effect required all three genes delivered as a polycistron within the same AAV particle — separate monocistronic viruses gave no effect on axon regeneration (Lu 2020, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2975-4). The functional endpoint came from a glaucoma model in which intraocular pressure was raised with microbeads for 21 days and the vector was injected only 3–4 weeks later, after axonal density and cell number had already significantly declined: OSK-treated glaucomatous eyes showed a restoration in axon density equivalent to that in the non-glaucomatous eyes and a significant increase in visual acuity relative to the pre-treatment baseline, restoring about half of visual acuity in the optomotor response assay, with a concordant improvement in the pattern electroretinogram (Lu 2020, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2975-4). The effect is not confined to mouse cells: nine days after damage, the neurite area was 15-fold greater in rejuvenated OSK-transduced human neurons than in controls, and that recovery was blocked by Tet2 knockdown but not by mTOR inhibition with rapamycin (Lu 2020, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2975-4). For scale against the alternative route to the same endpoint, conditional deletion of the growth suppressor PTEN in adult mouse retinal ganglion cells left around 45% surviving two weeks after injury versus around 20% in controls, with 8 to 10% of survivors regenerating axons beyond 0.5 mm and some extending beyond 3 mm (Park 2008, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1161566).
Highest Evidence Tier: T6 (mouse gene therapy with functional vision endpoints in two injury models, human neurons in vitro, plus an actively recruiting first-in-human Phase 1 of the same three-factor construct)
Translational Gaps: The human study is a single-dose Phase 1 whose stated endpoints are safety and tolerability in 18 participants (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07290244), so no efficacy claim exists in humans and none should be read into it. All the animal efficacy data are eye-only; every other tissue is untested by this delivery route. The nonhuman-primate data on non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy that supported the investigational new drug application were presented at company conferences rather than published as a peer-reviewed paper with an extractable effect size, so the strongest primate evidence cannot be cited to a DOI and this exhibit says so rather than implying published primate efficacy. The failure in 18-month-old mice is unexplained and it matters, because glaucoma and ischemic optic neuropathy are diseases of older people; the upper age boundary of the intervention has not been mapped. Expression also has to be gated, which means the therapy depends on a companion small molecule: participants take systemic doxycycline for 8 weeks to switch the factors on. The trial follows participants for up to 5 years precisely because the long-term consequences of persistent reprogramming factor expression in the human retina have not been measured.
Key References (DOIs): Lu Nature 2020 https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2975-4 | Park Science 2008 https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1161566 | Sun Nature 2011 https://doi.org/10.1038/nature10594 | Karg Cellular Reprogramming 2023 https://doi.org/10.1089/cell.2023.0074
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: The effect depends on active demethylation rather than generic growth-factor signalling, and the authors pinned that down genetically: knocking down either TET1 or TET2 blocks OSK's ability to raise Stat3 messenger RNA, promote retinal ganglion cell survival and support axon regeneration (Lu 2020, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2975-4). Stoichiometry is not a detail — co-delivering the three factors in separate monocistronic viruses produced no effect on axon regeneration at all, so anyone reproducing this must use a single polycistronic construct. On safety, after 10–18 months of continuous OSK induction the authors observed no increase in tumour incidence, which is the reassuring counterweight to the fact that continuous expression of all four factors in normal mice often induces teratomas or is fatal within days; AAV9 was chosen for the systemic long-term arm specifically because its weak tropism for the digestive system avoids the dysplasia and weight loss seen in transgenic models. One number is easy to misread and should not be: 'restoring about half of visual acuity' is a return toward the pre-treatment baseline in the microbead glaucoma model, not a doubling of normal vision. The direction check on the trial is clean — ER-100 administers OSK as the therapy, in the same pro-regenerative direction this library frames it, and the registry record states that it does not alter the participant's existing genes (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07290244). The PTEN comparison (Park 2008, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1161566) is included as a benchmark effect size for the same optic-nerve-crush assay, not as a candidate enhancement: PTEN loss is a tumour-suppressor knockout and was rejected as a standalone card for that reason. The reviewed UniProt accession used here, P20263, is the mouse Pou5f1 (OCT4) entry, matching the species of the experiments; the human Phase 1 uses the human orthologs of all three factors.

Manipulation: Co-expression of the parietal-eye opsin pair (parietopsin + pinopsin) with Go-alpha in a single photoreceptor
Narrative: Many lizards carry a third eye. On top of the skull, under a translucent scale, sits the parietal eye: a small structure with a lens and a retina, wired to the pineal complex rather than to the visual brain, and incapable of forming an image. What it does instead is measure colour. Su and colleagues (https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1123802) recorded in 2006 from single parietal-eye photoreceptors of the side-blotched lizard and found something no other vertebrate cell is known to do: the same cell answers green light by depolarizing and blue light by hyperpolarizing. Two opsins share one cell and pull its membrane potential in opposite directions, so the output is a ratio, the balance of blue against green overhead, rather than a count of photons. That ratio is exactly what swings at dawn and dusk, and an eye on the roof of the head is well placed to read it. The chemistry was pinned down in Osaka. Sakai and colleagues expressed lizard parietopsin in cultured cells, purified the pigment, and measured a green-sensitive absorption maximum at 522 nm, red-shifted relative to both rhodopsin and pinopsin, with a counterion arrangement closer to an invertebrate opsin than to a vertebrate one (https://doi.org/10.1021/bi2018283). Wada and colleagues then found the same 522 nm peak in iguana parietopsin, showing the tuning is a property of the molecule and not a quirk of one species (https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0039003). For a body, this is a colour comparator you could wear on your forehead: not a picture, but an instant read-out of the spectral quality of the light above you, of the kind a lizard uses to know where it stands in the day. Nothing like it has been transferred to a mammal, and the obstacle is wiring rather than optics, because the cell speaks a G-protein language the vertebrate retina does not understand.
Short Description: A small lensed eye set in the middle of the skull roof feeds photoreceptors that are wired two ways at once: green light drives a cell one direction and blue light drives the same cell the other, so it reports the colour of the sky rather than its brightness. The green pigment peaks at 522 nm and depolarizes the cell through Go-alpha, while the blue one hyperpolarizes it through gustducin-alpha. That pigment is dim by rod standards, with a photosensitivity 0.69 of bovine rhodopsin's, so the third eye collects less signal per photon than the eyes you already have. This has only ever been recorded in lizards, and no laboratory has put the opsin pair into a mammalian cell. The cascade also contains neither rod nor cone transducin-alpha, so it cannot plug into existing retinal wiring and needs an output nerve of its own.
Mechanism: The parietal-eye photoreceptor is the only vertebrate cell known to run two antagonistic phototransduction cascades at the same time. Green-sensitive parietopsin couples to Go-alpha, the alpha subunit of the Go class of heterotrimeric G proteins, and produces a depolarizing response, while blue-sensitive pinopsin couples to gustducin-alpha and produces a hyperpolarizing one. Neither rod nor cone transducin-alpha, the G protein that carries the signal in ordinary vertebrate photoreceptors, is present in the cell at all. Parietopsin's protonated retinal chromophore is stabilised by a counterion at Glu181 in the second extracellular loop, the arrangement typical of invertebrate opsins, rather than at the Glu113 position rhodopsin uses; Gln113 at that vacated site contributes to the pigment's red-shifted absorbance. Because both cascades converge on one membrane, the cell's voltage encodes the ratio of green to blue light instead of total intensity, which makes it a chromatic comparator rather than an intensity detector.
Achievements (effect sizes): Single-cell recordings from the parietal eye of the side-blotched lizard established that one photoreceptor can answer two colours in opposite directions, depolarizing to green light and hyperpolarizing to blue (Su 2006, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1123802). Recombinant work then measured the pigment itself. Lizard parietopsin expressed in cultured cells and purified showed an absorption maximum at 522 nm, which the authors single out as its noticeable characteristic, a red shift with respect to both rhodopsin and pinopsin (Sakai 2012, https://doi.org/10.1021/bi2018283). The same study asked how efficiently the pigment turns absorbed light into activation: photosensitivity at its 520 nm peak came to 0.69 +/- 0.02 of that of bovine rhodopsin at rhodopsin's own peak, and 0.63 +/- 0.02 when both pigments were compared at 500 nm. Its molar extinction coefficient, determined by acid denaturation against a bovine rhodopsin reference of 40600 M-1 cm-1, was 31700 +/- 500 M-1 cm-1 at 520 nm and 29000 +/- 500 M-1 cm-1 at 500 nm, so the pigment absorbs somewhat less strongly than rod pigment as well. An independent group repeating the measurement in a different lizard found iguana parietopsin peaking at 522 nm, almost identical to the side-blotched lizard's value, which makes the green tuning a property of the protein rather than of one animal (Wada 2012, https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0039003).
Highest Evidence Tier: T3 (native single-cell electrophysiology in lizard plus recombinant spectroscopy replicated in two lizard species and two laboratories; no mammalian transfer attempted)
Translational Gaps: No laboratory has yet expressed parietopsin, pinopsin and Go-alpha together in a mammalian photoreceptor or neuron and shown that the resulting cell answers two colours in opposite directions, so the central claim of this enhancement has never been tested outside a lizard. Parietal-eye photoreceptors also have a distinctive morphology of their own, and the intracellular messenger that carries the depolarizing arm of the cascade has not been fully identified, which means a builder would be copying a pathway whose middle step is still missing. Nobody knows whether a mammalian cell can hold two opposing opsin cascades without them cross-talking, and nobody knows what downstream circuit would interpret a bipolar voltage signal that no vertebrate visual pathway currently receives.
Key References (DOIs): Su Science 2006 https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1123802 | Sakai Biochemistry 2012 https://doi.org/10.1021/bi2018283 | Wada PLoS ONE 2012 https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0039003
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: The founding electrophysiology paper (Su 2006, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1123802) is closed-access, so the spectroscopic numbers in this record come from two sources read in full text: Sakai 2012 (https://doi.org/10.1021/bi2018283) and Wada 2012 (https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0039003). One internal inconsistency deserves flagging. The Biochemistry paper (https://doi.org/10.1021/bi2018283) also reports 495 nm as a wild-type value inside a pH-7.0 mutant comparison, whereas its own summary statement of parietopsin's characteristic absorption maximum is 522 nm; 522 nm is the figure used here. There is no experimental crystal or cryo-EM structure of parietopsin or of pinopsin, although AlphaFold models exist for lizard parietopsin (UniProt Q1L4C8, https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q1L4C8) and for pinopsin from the same species (UniProt Q1L4C7, https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q1L4C7). The trait has no commercial or clinical existence: no company and no registered trial. Bistable pineal opsins from this same family are being examined as optogenetic actuators, which is the most plausible near-term route by which these cascades would first reach a mammalian neuron.

Narrative: Heart disease is the world's top killer, and its chief accomplice is LDL cholesterol. For decades, statins have been the answer — but they require daily pills for life, and many patients stop taking them. Nature, however, has already solved the compliance problem. In 2006, Hobbs and Cohen discovered that roughly 3% of African Americans carry loss-of-function mutations in PCSK9, a liver enzyme that destroys LDL receptors. These carriers had LDL levels 28% lower and an 88% reduction in coronary heart disease — with no apparent downside. In 2021, Verve Therapeutics used lipid nanoparticle-delivered adenine base editing to knock out PCSK9 in cynomolgus monkeys with a single intravenous infusion: LDL dropped 59% and stayed down for over a year with no booster. In 2025, their phase Ib human trial (VERVE-102) showed durable 39–55% LDL reductions in heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia patients already on maximally tolerated therapy. One injection, permanent cholesterol lowering, no daily pills. The catch: liver base editing is irreversible — any off-target edits in hepatocytes are permanent, and the long-term cancer risk of widespread somatic editing remains theoretical but unquantified.
Short Description: Liver cells shred their own LDL receptors on orders from PCSK9; knock out that gene and receptors stay put, pulling cholesterol from blood for good. People born without working PCSK9 show LDL 28% lower and 88% less coronary disease over 15 years. A one-shot LNP base editor cut LDL 39–55% in a 2025 human trial (VERVE-102, familial hypercholesterolemia); Eli Lilly bought the program that year. The edit is permanent and liver-wide, so an off-target cut in a hepatocyte can't be undone.
Mechanism: Adenine base editor (ABE) delivered via LNP to hepatocytes; introduces A→G transition creating splice-site disruption in PCSK9 exon 1; loss of functional PCSK9 protein → LDL receptors on hepatocyte surface persist instead of being degraded → increased LDL-C clearance from plasma.
Achievements (effect sizes): Cohen 2006 NEJM: PCSK9 LOF carriers — LDL −28%, CHD risk −88% (15-year follow-up, n=3363 Black participants). Musunuru 2021 Nature (monkey, n=4): single LNP-ABE dose → PCSK9 protein −90%, LDL-C −59% at 8 months, stable. VERVE-102 2025 (phase Ib, n=12 HeFH): LDL reductions 39–55% at highest dose, durable through 180 days; no serious liver events.
Highest Evidence Tier: T5
Translational Gaps: Phase III efficacy/safety (MACE endpoints); long-term off-target somatic editing surveillance; immunogenicity of LNP on repeat dosing (if ever needed); applicability beyond FH to general population; liver cancer risk from widespread base editing.
Key References (DOIs): Cohen NEJM 2006 https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa054013 | Musunuru Nature 2021 https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03534-y | Verve Therapeutics 2025 AHA Late-Breaking https://doi.org/10.1056/nejmoa2601283
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: PCSK9-null humans (compound LOF homozygotes) are healthy, supporting safety — but sample size is tiny (2 reported individuals). LNP tropism is liver-dominant but not liver-exclusive; low-level editing in other organs is possible. Base editing off-targets are harder to detect than CRISPR indels. Cohen 2006 CHD reduction (88%) may overestimate causal effect due to lifelong exposure vs mid-life intervention. Verve trials use next-gen LNP (GalNAc-targeted) to improve hepatocyte specificity. COMMERCIAL STATUS: Verve Therapeutics (https://www.vervetx.com/), developer of VERVE-101/102, was acquired by Eli Lilly in June 2025, signalling major-pharma confidence in the approach. This is a regulated clinical program, not an alternative-jurisdiction therapy. The base-editing platform is not commercially available outside clinical trials.

Manipulation: Two-gene pathway transfer (neofunctionalised pyruvate decarboxylase + muscle alcohol dehydrogenase)
Narrative:
In northern Europe, shallow ponds freeze over and the water beneath the ice runs out of oxygen completely for months. Almost nothing with a spine survives that. Crucian carp not only survive it, they stay active - and unlike the anoxia-tolerant freshwater turtles, which go still and wait, the fish keeps swimming (https://doi.org/10.1242/jeb.00979). The reason is that its muscle ferments glucose to ethanol rather than to lactate, and the ethanol simply diffuses out of the gills into the pond. Because the anaerobic end product leaves the body as a neutral molecule instead of piling up as acid, glycolysis can run indefinitely without the lactic acidosis that kills other vertebrates in minutes.

In 2017 a group at the University of Oslo worked out the machinery (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-07385-4). A whole-genome duplication in the genus Carassius left spare copies of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, and one pair of E1 subunits was repurposed into a pyruvate decarboxylase - the first ever described in a vertebrate, performing the same chemistry brewer's yeast uses. A single amino-acid change, betaD319N, breaks the salt bridge that would normally dock that subunit onto the complex core, so it works detached and releases acetaldehyde instead of feeding acetyl-CoA into respiration. A muscle-specific alcohol dehydrogenase, ADH8a, then reduces the acetaldehyde to ethanol. The fish gets away with it because tetraploidy let it keep an intact, normally functioning complex encoded on the other gene copy, and because it confines the whole arrangement to skeletal muscle.

The uncomfortable detail is that betaD319N is the substitution associated with pyruvate dehydrogenase complex dysfunction in human cells. What is an elegant solution in a tetraploid fish with gills is, in a diploid land animal, a metabolic disease allele plus ethanol with nowhere to leave.
Short Description: With no oxygen at all, muscle stops making lactic acid and brews ethanol instead, which diffuses out across the gills - so the blood never acidifies and the animal keeps swimming rather than shutting down. Crucian carp run this for up to four to five months a year under ice, carrying up to 7 micromol of ethanol per gram of red muscle, while the closely related common carp cannot make ethanol and dies within hours of true anoxia. It takes two genes in a precise arrangement: a duplicated pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 subunit bearing the betaD319N substitution, expressed at over 60-fold excess over the complex core in skeletal muscle only, plus a muscle alcohol dehydrogenase. Nobody has transferred the pathway into another animal; the case rests on comparative genomics in the fish. On land the ethanol has nowhere to go, and betaD319N is the same change associated with pyruvate dehydrogenase complex dysfunction in human cells.
Mechanism: A whole-genome duplication in the genus Carassius left spare copies of the subunits of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDH complex), the mitochondrial machine that normally converts pyruvate into acetyl-coenzyme A for aerobic respiration. One pair of E1 paralogs, E1alpha3 together with E1beta2, neofunctionalised into a pyruvate decarboxylase (PDC) - the first described in any vertebrate and analogous to the enzyme brewer's yeast uses - which releases acetaldehyde from pyruvate instead of channelling it into acetyl-CoA. The enabling change is the substitution betaD319N in E1beta2, absent from the E1beta1 copy, which abolishes a salt bridge to lysine residues on the E2 core of the complex so that the E1 unit operates physically detached from it. A muscle-specific alcohol dehydrogenase, ADH8a, then reduces the acetaldehyde to ethanol, and the ethanol diffuses freely across the gills into the surrounding water. Because the terminal product of anaerobic glycolysis leaves the body as a neutral small molecule rather than accumulating as lactate, glycolysis can continue indefinitely without lactic acidosis.
Achievements (effect sizes): Transcript profiling across crucian carp tissues showed that in red and white skeletal muscles, total E1:E2 and E1:E3 transcript ratios were significantly higher by a factor greater than 60 compared to all other, non-ethanol producing tissues such as brain, heart and liver - the evidence that a free, complex-independent E1 exists specifically in the muscle that makes ethanol (Fagernes 2017, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-07385-4). The same study identified the enabling mutation and showed why it works: the amino acid substitution betaD319N, which molecular modelling places at a salt bridge between betaD319 and lysine 362 on the E2 core, produces a greater than 100-fold increase in the dissociation constant between E1 and E2 and a concomitant decrease in in vitro pyruvate dehydrogenase complex activity, and the substitution appears to be unique to the ethanol-producing goldfish and crucian carp and is not found in any other species investigated. That substitution was independently confirmed in the sequence databases, where E1beta2 carries asparagine at position 319 (UniProt A0A288DUG2, https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/A0A288DUG2) while E1beta1 carries aspartate there (UniProt A0A288DSR4, https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/A0A288DSR4). The physiological magnitude is large and sustained: the fish reaches elevated tissue ethanol concentrations reaching up to 7 micromol/g in red muscle during anoxia for up to 4-5 months of the year (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-07385-4), and it survives for months in completely oxygen-deprived freshwater habitats, also tolerating a few days of anoxia at room temperature and, unlike anoxia-tolerant freshwater turtles, remaining physically active while anoxic (Nilsson & Renshaw 2004, https://doi.org/10.1242/jeb.00979).
Highest Evidence Tier: T3 (comparative genomics, transcript quantification and structural modelling in the native species; no heterologous reconstitution of the two-gene pathway)
Translational Gaps: Nobody has transferred the two genes into a heterologous animal and measured anoxic survival, so the gain-of-function claim rests entirely on comparative evidence: Carassius has the pathway and survives months of anoxia, while common carp lacks it and dies within hours (Fagernes 2017, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-07385-4). Reconstituting it would require more than putting two genes into a host, because the pathway depends on tissue-restricted expression at a more than 60-fold excess of E1 over the E2 and E3 core components in muscle alone; expressing the decarboxylase everywhere would compromise aerobic pyruvate oxidation in every tissue that got it. There is also no route for the product. A carp voids ethanol across its gills into open water, and a terrestrial body has no comparable diffusive sink, so the recipient would have to clear months of continuous ethanol through the liver instead. No experimental structure exists for the carp subunits; only predicted models are available.
Key References (DOIs): Fagernes Scientific Reports 2017 https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-07385-4 | Nilsson Journal of Experimental Biology 2004 https://doi.org/10.1242/jeb.00979
Notes (limitations, contradictions, cave: The natural negative control is stated in the same paper and is unusually clean: common carp tolerates severe hypoxia but dies within hours of anoxia, apparently because lactate accumulates in the absence of any ethanol route (Fagernes 2017, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-07385-4). The accessions were checked directly against UniProt for this entry - A0A288DSR4 (E1beta1, 359 amino acids) carries aspartate at position 319 while A0A288DUG2 (E1beta2, 360 amino acids) carries asparagine (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/A0A288DUG2). There are no clinical trials, no registry records and no products; the authors instead propose Carassius as a model organism for chronic ethanol exposure and for hypoxia and ischaemia research (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-017-07385-4). Note the direction of the human literature on betaD319N: in people the same substitution is discussed as a cause of pyruvate dehydrogenase complex dysfunction, so a change that reads as an enhancement in a fish is catalogued as pathology in a human, and this card should be read as a species-specific solution rather than a portable upgrade.
